record.title: DepthGraft reports hierarchical cross-layer KV reconstruction with lower cache and prefill cost
record.summary: The authors propose hierarchical sharing of key/value (KV) representations across transformer depth, reconstructing deep-layer KV from aligned shallow and middle layers. In experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters, they report a roughly one-third KV-cache reduction. For 9B MLA and 16B GQA models, the paper reports lower time-to-first-token (TTFT) at 8K–128K context and nearly unchanged time-per-output-token (TPOT); at 128K, reported TTFT reductions are 26.8% and 28.8%, respectively. These results are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that DepthGraft reduces KV-cache use by roughly one third while retaining prefill early completion.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: At 128K context, the authors report TTFT reductions of 26.8% on 9B MLA and 28.8% on 16B GQA, while TPOT remains within 1% of baseline across tested lengths.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For a 16B GQA MoE, the paper reports MMLU-Pro increasing from 23.86 to 30.86, an absolute gain of 7.00 points versus its GQA baseline.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish independent reproduction, production deployment, or transfer to arbitrary model families and workloads.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of reported quality, KV-cache or latency results was located or performed; linked code was not inspected.
The paper does not establish whether the reported benefits transfer to other architectures, production serving stacks or workload distributions.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported quality and efficiency results generalize, reducing KV-cache capacity by about one third while lowering long-context prefill latency could materially change inference memory planning and serving design. The score is limited to author-reported results on selected 0.5B–16B dense/MoE models; no production or independent validation is established.
limitations: The performance and latency results are reported by the paper authors and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The long-context latency comparison is limited to 9B MLA and 16B GQA configurations, contexts of 8K–128K, and a fixed 2K generation length.
The reported 16B MMLU-Pro gain is a within-paper benchmark result; no independent evaluation, error bars or multi-seed reproduction was inspected.
The linked project code and detailed evaluation artifacts were not inspected or run; production deployment and serving economics are not established.
brief.summary: The authors propose hierarchical sharing of key/value (KV) representations across transformer depth, reconstructing deep-layer KV from aligned shallow and middle layers. In experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters, they report a roughly one-third KV-cache reduction. For 9B MLA and 16B GQA models, the paper reports lower time-to-first-token (TTFT) at 8K–128K context and nearly unchanged time-per-output-token (TPOT); at 128K, reported TTFT reductions are 26.8% and 28.8%, respectively. These results are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report roughly one-third lower KV-cache use, consistent benchmark gains in dense and MoE models, and lower long-context TTFT with TPOT within 1% of baseline on the tested configurations. In the 16B GQA MoE table, MMLU-Pro rises from 23.86 to 30.86 (+7.00 points).
technical.compute_or_cost: The authors report about one-third lower KV cache and TTFT reductions at 128K of 26.8% on 9B MLA and 28.8% on 16B GQA. Training throughput is reported as essentially identical. No independent hardware-cost or production economics measurement was performed.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint and its tables are directly inspectable. Experimental performance and efficiency outcomes remain author-reported claims and were not independently reproduced.
technical.implementation_status: The paper links a project repository; this activation did not inspect or run it.
technical.mechanism: Deep layers reconstruct KV from stride-aligned shallow and middle source pairs. Reuse removes independent deep-layer KV projections and cache tensors; the authors argue shared KV edges also create cross-layer gradient paths that regularize representation geometry.
technical.novelty: Hierarchical cross-layer KV reconstruction is presented as both a cache-saving mechanism and a structural training regularizer through distributed cross-layer gradient flow.
technical.regime: Dense models at 0.5B–1.5B and MoE models at 3B–16B total parameters; long-context inference reported for 9B MLA and 16B GQA at 8K–128K context with fixed 2K generation length.
technical.reproducibility: Full arXiv v1 PDF inspected, including Tables 2–3. No independent reproduction was found or attempted; project code and detailed evaluation artifacts were not inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within-paper GQA baselines on the same reported model settings, plus a 9B MLA baseline for long-context latency. The paper also compares adjacent and global-anchor KV-sharing variants in ablations.

brief.title: DepthGraft reports hierarchical cross-layer KV reconstruction with lower cache and prefill cost
brief.why_it_matters: If reproduced, cross-layer KV reconstruction could reduce inference memory and prefill latency while retaining benchmark performance, affecting long-context model and serving architecture choices. The evidence is a single paper’s experiments and does not establish production deployment, broad model-family transfer or independently verified quality gains.
